Fri

Jul 31High confidenceoutbound · 06:00–22:00 ET
METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KLZU observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. KLZU has no TAF station, so KPDK is used as a proxy. It is the strongest flight-category evidence this page can show. A KPDK proxy TAF group covers part of this day.NWS-hrNWS hourly gridpoint forecast — the National Weather Service digital forecast for the grid cell containing KLZU, updated through the day and reaching about 156 hours. It gives hour-by-hour sky, wind and precipitation probability, and it is the spine of the change windows on this board. The NWS hourly gridpoint forecast reaches this day.NWS-dayNWS day/night outlook — the same National Weather Service grid summarised into day and night halves, reaching about 168 hours. Coarser than the hourly product but it covers one day further, so this page uses it only to describe spans the hourly forecast cannot reach. Not needed: this day is already covered by the finer-resolution hourly gridpoint forecast.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued by the National Weather Service four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this page uses it to corroborate the flight category. A GFS MAV MOS row corroborates the flight category on this day.MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This page shows it only as a flagged outlook and never promotes it into a short-range category. This day is already covered by finer-resolution sources.GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAMs were read for KLZU this run.

METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KLZU observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. KLZU has no TAF station, so KPDK is used as a proxy. It is the strongest flight-category evidence this page can show. Beyond the TAF horizon of about 30 hours; no TAF exists at this range for any station.NWS-hrNWS hourly gridpoint forecast — the National Weather Service digital forecast for the grid cell containing KLZU, updated through the day and reaching about 156 hours. It gives hour-by-hour sky, wind and precipitation probability, and it is the spine of the change windows on this board. The NWS hourly gridpoint forecast reaches this day.NWS-dayNWS day/night outlook — the same National Weather Service grid summarised into day and night halves, reaching about 168 hours. Coarser than the hourly product but it covers one day further, so this page uses it only to describe spans the hourly forecast cannot reach. Not needed: this day is already covered by the finer-resolution hourly gridpoint forecast.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued by the National Weather Service four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this page uses it to corroborate the flight category. Beyond the GFS MAV MOS horizon of about 72 hours, or no MAV row carried both a ceiling and a visibility for this day.MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This page shows it only as a flagged outlook and never promotes it into a short-range category. This day is already covered by finer-resolution sources.GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAMs were read for KLZU this run.

Short term

.. (Today through Friday) Issued at 450 AM EDT Thu Jul 30 2026 An overall less active pattern is expected through the short term. For the afternoon, less oppressive temperatures are expected for most of the CWA. Highs in the upper 80s and low 90s but with dewpoints in the 60s making it feel a lot more comfortable than what we've seen over the past few days. This trend will continue as we go into the second half of the work week, with pleasant temperatures and minimal chances of afternoon thunderstorms over the next 36 hours. Storms return to the forecast on Saturday morning as another front moves in from the west.

Long term

.. (Friday night through Wednesday) Issued at 450 AM EDT Thu Jul 30 2026 The long-term forecast period will be characterized primarily by a sharp increase in overall rain chances as well as a general decrease in afternoon high temperatures amid more widespread cloud cover and convection. An upper trough will dig into the eastern CONUS by Saturday, sending a surface low into the Ohio Valley and its attendant frontal boundary into the forecast area. This will send deep tropical moisture streaming quickly back northward into the area after the brief reprieve we will have experienced late this week. With PWATs forecast to surge back into the 2 - 2.25" range by Saturday, widespread showers and thunderstorms are expected. While the severe threat currently looks rather limited, locally heavy rainfall will be a concern given the environment, and as such WPC already has a "Marginal" Excessive Rainfall out for our area on Saturday. The front is progged to make gradual progress into the area on Sunday, keeping PoPs quite high in advance. Again, locally heavy rainfall will remain the primary concern. Additionally, a weak upper low looks develop within the trough axis that will bisect the forecast area by late weekend into early next week. As such, while the surface front will gradually push eastward and wash out, the presence of the weak meandering upper low should provide sufficient lift for continued scattered diurnally-enhanced convection through early next week before upper riding looks to make a gradual return thereafter. As mentioned above, more widespread cloud cover/rainfall will keep high temperatures more tempered in the 80s to perhaps low 90s, though overnight lows will creep back into the 70s.

This trend will continue as we go into the second half of the work

forecast area by late weekend into early next week. As such, while

presence of the weak meandering upper low should provide sufficient 
lift for continued scattered diurnally-enhanced convection through

KROA OBS - VFR Roanoke Rgnl, VA, US · Roanoke valleyETE1h56Dist279 nm
METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KROA observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. A TAF was read for this airport this run (state: partial).MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAMs were read for KROA this run.

KSHD OBS - VFR Staunton/Shenandoah Valley Rgnl, VA, US · Shenandoah valleyETE2h25Dist355 nm
METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KSHD observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. A TAF was read for this airport this run (state: partial). This airport has no TAF station of its own, so KCHO is used as a proxy; that is a normal condition, not a failure.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAMs were read for KSHD this run.

KSAV OBS - VFR Savannah Intl, GA, US · historic coastETE1h15Dist178 nm
METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KSAV observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. A TAF was read for this airport this run (state: partial).MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAMs were read for KSAV this run.

KJZI OBS - VFR Charleston Exec, SC, US · Charleston ExecETE1h28Dist213 nm
METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KJZI observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. A TAF was read for this airport this run (state: partial).MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAMs were read for KJZI this run.

KHXD OBS - VFR Hilton Head Arpt, SC, US · Hilton HeadETE1h21Dist195 nm
METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KHXD observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. A TAF was read for this airport this run (state: partial). This airport has no TAF station of its own, so KSAV is used as a proxy; that is a normal condition, not a failure.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAMs were read for KHXD this run.

KFIN OBS - VFR Palm Coast/Flagler Exec, FL, US · Flagler Exec FLETE2h03Dist295 nm
METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KFIN observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. A TAF was read for this airport this run (state: partial). This airport has no TAF station of its own, so KDAB is used as a proxy; that is a normal condition, not a failure.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAMs were read for KFIN this run.

METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KCRE observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. A TAF was read for this airport this run (state: partial). This airport has no TAF station of its own, so KMYR is used as a proxy; that is a normal condition, not a failure.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAMs were read for KCRE this run.

Gulf East

KECP OBS - VFR Panama City/NW Florida Beaches Intl, FL, US · Panama City BeachETE1h38Dist237 nm
METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KECP observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. A TAF was read for this airport this run (state: partial).MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAMs were read for KECP this run.

KPNS OBS - VFR Pensacola Intl, FL, US · Pensacola (Class C)ETE1h51Dist267 nm
METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KPNS observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. A TAF was read for this airport this run (state: partial).MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAMs were read for KPNS this run.

KDAB OBS - VFR Daytona Beach Intl, FL, US · Daytona Beach (Class C)ETE2h13Dist324 nm
METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KDAB observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. A TAF was read for this airport this run (state: partial).MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAMs were read for KDAB this run.

METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KTPF observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. A TAF was read for this airport this run (state: partial). This airport has no TAF station of its own, so KTPA is used as a proxy; that is a normal condition, not a failure.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KSRQ observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. A TAF was read for this airport this run (state: partial).MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAMs were read for KSRQ this run.

Gulf West

KJKA OBS - VFR Gulf Shores/Edwards Arpt, AL, US · Gulf Shores ALETE2h01Dist291 nm
METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KJKA observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. A TAF was read for this airport this run (state: partial).MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAMs were read for KJKA this run.

KBFM OBS - VFR Mobile/Downtown Arpt, AL, US · Mobile DowntownETE2h00Dist290 nm
METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KBFM observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. A TAF was read for this airport this run (state: partial).MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. The NOTAM query failed this run (state: RATE_LIMITED), so the NOTAM list is unknown rather than empty.

METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KHSA observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. A TAF was read for this airport this run (state: partial). This airport has no TAF station of its own, so KGPT is used as a proxy; that is a normal condition, not a failure.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. The NOTAM query failed this run (state: RATE_LIMITED), so the NOTAM list is unknown rather than empty.

KOPF OBS - VFR Miami/Opa Locka Arpt, FL, US · Miami-Opa LockaETE3h30Dist521 nm
METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KOPF observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. A TAF was read for this airport this run (state: partial).MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAMs were read for KOPF this run.

KHPN OBS - IFR White Plains/Westchester Cnty, NY, US · White Plains NYETE4h18Dist647 nm
METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KHPN observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. A TAF was read for this airport this run (state: partial).MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAMs were read for KHPN this run.

3 · Hazard feeds & regional observations

Unfiltered hazard feeds (not route-geometry screened): 13 SIGMET records, 30 G-AIRMET records, 2 CWA records. Regional current observations (not corridor forecasts): Mountain: IFR/LIFR at KTRI; Mountain: MVFR at KGKT; Atlantic South: IFR/LIFR at KSGJ; Gulf East: MVFR at KSRQ.
Scope: Hazard counts are raw feed totals and have not been filtered against a proposed route, altitude, or time. Airport flight categories are current point observations, not corridor forecasts.

4 · Planning gates

  • Evidence gate: an unavailable, stale, or out-of-horizon source is unknown — never treat it as favorable.
  • Weather gate: compare current observations and valid-period forecasts with personal ceiling, visibility, convection, wind, and crosswind minimums.
  • Route gate: screen the actual route, altitude, and time against official hazard products; feed totals on this page are not route-filtered.
  • Operations gate: verify NOTAMs, TFRs, runway conditions, fuel, aircraft performance, daylight, and alternates.

5 · ForeFlight manual cross-check (before flight)

  • Official briefing matches these go/no-go windows
  • Prog charts / radar / satellite trend agrees with convection timing
  • Winds & temps aloft along actual route (may shift ETE)
  • NOTAMs & TFRs — airport-scoped NMS records may be shown, but route-wide/TFR coverage is not included; pull a fresh official briefing for departure, destination, and alternates
  • Runway condition / length / closures at destination & alternate
  • Weight & balance + performance at forecast density altitude (heat!)
  • File & brief in ForeFlight; confirm fuel stops if long-range

★ Features

Available now

  • Per-source state, validity horizon, and target-date coverage for every destination
  • Explicit unavailable/out-of-horizon target cells; no static weather fallback
  • Per-airport expandable detail — current observations, covered forecasts, dep/dest METAR temperatures
  • Four-day KLZU change-window board with four outbound/return planning alternatives
  • Source-labelled TAF/MOS flight-category guidance only when a source interval actually covers the planned window — a day with no covering interval shows an explicit unavailable/out-of-horizon state instead of a category, never an implied one
  • Timed NWS weather, wind-favored runway (magnetic, from each airport's own runways), gust, and material crosswind context wherever the forecast supplies them
  • Raw METAR/TAF + data-sources dropdown per airport
  • FAA Airport Status & Delays with known, unsupported, and unavailable states
  • Best-effort 100LL fuel prices
  • Auto-refreshed about 4x a day by an hourly scheduler that republishes once 6 h have passed since the last publish, so refresh times drift; the last-updated stamp is exact and the next-run stamp is an estimate
  • Quick links (Flight Circle, ForeFlight, FlightAware) + Feedback
  • FAA chart-cycle stamp (current VFR Sectional + Chart Supplement)
  • Download PDF — print-ready, color-preserving (semantic colors kept on paper)
  • Deterministic evidence-backed page; external AI aviation prose is withheld pending a validated evidence schema, so the executive-summary region shows an explicit pending-feature placeholder instead of generated text
  • Model-labeled MOS target-window outlook per airport (Iowa State GFS with conditional GFS Extended/MEX), with runtime and validity horizon shown
  • Expandable NWS FFC pattern summary and extended outlook inside the KLZU board
  • Per-airport chart links: SkyVector & AirNav/Chart Supplement (deep links)
  • FAA NMS Pre-Production (sandbox) NOTAM adapter with explicit per-airport source states; active on this page with non-operational Pre-Production test data, and never a substitute for an official briefing
  • Full run archive: run_manifest.json with all data + provenance log
